title: Kremlin propagandists brace for US inauguration
text: EUvsDisinfo – analiza: Kremlin propagandists brace for US inauguration. As the US prepares for the inauguration of its new president, Russian outlets have been busy crafting stories challenging NATO, criticising Western unity, and promoting Russian interests. Kremlin propaganda has been rife with fantasies about hypothetical US wars of aggression against Canada and attacks on Greenland. Russian TV propagandist Vladimir Solovyov recently used these Kremlin narratives to justify calls for the restoration of all Soviet territory. Russian outlets have gleefully portrayed the incoming US administration as a potential source of division within the transatlantic community and of a weakened or possibly even dismantled NATO. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov recently compared a potential referendum in Greenland with the illegal annexation referendums in the Ukrainian regions of Kherson, Zaporizhzhia, Luhansk and Donetsk, pretending that these manipulated shows , held at Russian gun-point in September 2022 in the midst of war and deportation, were trustworthy local expressions. Tempered ‘realism’ At a recent press conference, Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov, however, offered quite a measured comment , saying, ‘If Mr. Donald Trump aims to make America great again after taking office, we will have to closely monitor the methods he uses to achieve that goal’. RT’s chief propagandist, Margarita Simonyan, also appeared to temper her excitement about what the new US administration could mean for Russia’s war of aggression. In a recent interview , she suggested that ‘it is realistic that both Trump and [Russia] could agree that we stop at the line of contact [frontlines in Ukraine]. Everything on our side of the line would be ours’. As she preached ‘realism’ or the Kremlin trope ‘realities on the ground’, she expressed disappointment, adding, ‘Of course, I would want Odesa, Kyiv, Kharkiv, and everything else’. Her statements quickly led to criticism from war hawks in Russia: ‘ Why should the realisation of the objectives of the special military operation be tied to events in American domestic politics?’, some of them asked . Russian outlets abuzz with hopes for a Trump-Putin summit The prevailing narrative from Moscow, however, has been that the incoming US administration will display political astuteness and may challenge transatlantic relations, while Russian outlets have been abuzz with talks of a potential high-level meeting between Putin and Trump.
